question: What is the primary purpose of psychiatric follow-up care in the community?

options.A: Issuing permanent discharge certificates from hospital
options.B: Preventing relapse and maintaining patient stability
options.C: Conducting forensic psychological testing for courts
options.D: Providing temporary shelter for homeless psychiatric clients

explanation: Follow-up care focuses on continuous monitoring and support to keep patients stable outside the hospital. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T5#GNS314_U4_T5_h1)

question: Why is regular community follow-up considered vital after psychiatric discharge?

options.A: Government policy mandates weekly visits for all citizens
options.B: Patients often face triggers that can cause rapid symptom relapse
options.C: Hospitals require beds to be cleared for new surgical cases
options.D: Clients completely forget their diagnosis upon leaving the ward

explanation: Returning to community stressors without support frequently leads to worsening mental health status. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T5#GNS314_U4_T5_h1)

question: Who serves as the primary bridge between hospital care and the patient's home?
explanation: Community psychiatric nurses directly link hospital treatment teams with home-based recovery support. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T5#GNS314_U4_T5_h2)

question: A community nurse notices a patient is isolating more during a home visit. What action shows correct clinical reasoning?

options.A: Discontinue all home visits to encourage self-reliance
options.B: Advise the family to lock the patient inside the room
options.C: Explore potential triggers and report the behavioral shift
options.D: Wait until the next scheduled annual clinic appointment

explanation: Early identification of withdrawal helps prevent a full relapse through timely intervention. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T5#GNS314_U4_T5_h2)

question: What is the best way to evaluate a returning psychiatric patient's progress?

options.A: Compare current findings against the patient's previous baseline
options.B: Measure their performance against a strict population average
options.C: Rely solely on what the landlord reports about them
options.D: Check their school or work report cards from childhood

explanation: Individualized tracking against a personal baseline reveals meaningful changes in mental status. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T5#GNS314_U4_T5_h3)

question: Why should nurses document specific behavioral observations instead of vague terms?

options.A: Patients demand to read their charts word for word daily
options.B: It provides objective data for the whole healthcare team to review
options.C: Vague descriptions are illegal under standard nursing acts
options.D: Hospital management requires lengthy paperwork for every shift

explanation: Clear, objective notes ensure accurate tracking and communication among multidisciplinary team members. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T5#GNS314_U4_T5_h3)

question: What is a leading cause of psychiatric re-hospitalization in community settings?

options.A: Participating in routine community social clubs
options.B: Excessive consumption of clean drinking water
options.C: Attending vocational training programs too early

explanation: Stopping or skipping psychotropic drugs frequently precipitates a return of acute symptoms. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T5#GNS314_U4_T5_h4)

question: A patient complains that antipsychotic drugs cause severe muscle stiffness. What is the appropriate nursing action?

options.A: Tell the patient to stop taking all medications immediately
options.B: Ignore the complaint because drugs always cause discomfort
options.C: Advise the client to double the next dose for tolerance
options.D: Assess the side effect and report it to the prescriber

explanation: Addressing distressing side effects prevents outright medication abandonment and builds trust. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T5#GNS314_U4_T5_h4)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common early warning sign of psychiatric relapse?

options.A: Neglecting basic personal hygiene and grooming
options.B: Sudden and severe onset of sleep disturbances
options.C: Marked withdrawal from family and friends
options.D: Consistently sleeping eight hours every night

explanation: Normal, healthy sleep patterns indicate stability, whereas sleep disruption points toward relapse. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T5#GNS314_U4_T5_h5)

question: Why is identifying a patient's personal warning signs crucial for follow-up care?

options.A: It eliminates the need for any future clinic visits
options.B: It helps the family calculate exact medication costs
options.C: It proves the patient is fully cured of the illness
options.D: It allows intervention before an acute crisis occurs

explanation: Catching early symptoms lets the care team adjust treatment before full hospitalization becomes necessary. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T5#GNS314_U4_T5_h5)

question: Which professional typically assists with financial and housing needs during community care?
explanation: Social workers specialize in addressing the socioeconomic barriers affecting patient recovery. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T5#GNS314_U4_T5_h6)

question: Why is involving multiple disciplines important for long-term mental health recovery?

options.A: Nurses are not qualified to speak with patients about daily life
options.B: Family members refuse to talk to anyone except medical doctors
options.C: Hospital regulations require every department to sign discharge papers
options.D: Patients have diverse needs spanning medical, social, and economic areas

explanation: Comprehensive care addresses every facet of a client's life to prevent relapse and promote functioning. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T5#GNS314_U4_T5_h6)

question: What major barrier often prevents Nigerian patients from attending distant psychiatric review clinics?

options.A: Universal free ambulance services in rural zones
options.B: Transportation costs and long travel distances
options.C: Excessive availability of community mental health nurses
options.D: Mandatory daily check-ins at local police stations

explanation: Financial constraints and poor transport infrastructure make reaching distant urban clinics difficult. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T5#GNS314_U4_T5_h7)

question: How should a community psychiatric nurse respond to the widespread use of traditional healers?

options.A: Engage in respectful dialogue and collaborative referral pathways
options.B: Threaten clients with police arrest if they miss clinic appointments
options.C: Ignore traditional practices and pretend they do not exist
options.D: Condemn all families who visit alternative healing centers

explanation: Building bridges with alternative healers helps ensure patient safety and encourages orthodox care linkage. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T5#GNS314_U4_T5_h7)
